title: Russia’s Arrest of a Japanese Journalist Deepens the Freeze in Japan-Russia Relations
author: Takahashi Kosuke
text:
Credit: Depositphotos
Russia’s detention of a Japanese journalist on espionage allegations has triggered a diplomatic protest from Tokyo and raised fresh concerns about press freedom, threatening to further strain relations between Japan and Russia amid the ongoing war in Ukraine and their longstanding territorial dispute.On October 13, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) announced that it had detained a correspondent for Japan’s Hokkaido Shimbun in the Far Eastern Sakhalin region. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova identified the journalist as Imai Yuki. Russian authorities said he was apprehended a day before his planned departure from Russia and transferred to Moscow, where a court ordered his detention until December 12. Espionage convictions in Russia can carry prison terms of up to 20 years.[...]
